extracted.intended_audience: patent researchers, historians, librarians, and archivists
extracted.subtask_description: Create or interpret an alphabetical index of United States patents issued in 1877, listing each patentee with key bibliographic metadata (name, residence, invention title, date, volume, Gazette reference, patent number). Useful for historical research and patent lookup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphabetical list of patentees for the year 1877
rubrics_metrics.description: Alphabetical list of patentees for the year 1877.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize the index entries in strict alphabetical order by patentee surname; group all entries for that year together under that ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name, residence, and invention
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each entry should include the patentee's full name, residence (city, state or country), and a concise title or short description of the invention (e.g., 'Dennison, Albert S., Watertown, N. Y. Paper bag'). Use the same compact format consistently across entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the patent issue date for each entry, using the abbreviated month-day-year form as shown (e.g., 'Dec. 25, 1877'). Place the date in its own column or clearly associated position for easy reading and sorting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly volume
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the monthly volume reference (numeric) associated with the patent issue; display it in its designated column to link the entry to the corresponding monthly publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette reference
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the Official Gazette page or issue reference for each patent entry so readers can locate the published notice. Present this consistently in the Gazette column.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent number (No.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the patent number for each entry (the official patent issue number). Present this in a dedicated 'No.' column to allow direct lookup of the patent document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate assignor/assignee relationships and reissue status
rubrics_metrics.description: Parenthetical notes such as '(See ... assignor.)' and '(Reissue.)' appear alongside entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relevant, include parenthetical annotations indicating assignment (assignor/assignee) and reissued patents. Use cross-references '(See X, assignor.)' where an entry's interest is assigned to another party, and mark reissues explicitly with '(Reissue.)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'Same' and cross-references for repeated or related entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of 'Same' and 'See' appears to indicate repeated information or references to related entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple consecutive entries refer to the same residence/invention/assignee, the index may use 'Same' to avoid repetition; use explicit 'See' cross-references to direct the reader to the primary related entry. Maintain clarity so readers can follow which entries are duplicates or cross-referenced.
